acceptance: Hardware key defined and recorded in the ADR: CPU model plus logical core count for self-run results; for managed services the recorded service tier or warehouse size; results with neither are unranked and labelled 'hardware not recorded'.

The explorer pipeline and site rankings group cohorts by benchmark, scale, phase, tuning mode and hardware key; a test with bundles on two CPU models shows two cohorts; a test shows a result without a key is unranked with the label.
Before and after counts recorded on this item: ranked results, cohorts, and cohorts below the 3-identity minimum.

ADR status changes from provisional to accepted for answers 1-12, with 7 rewritten for the hardware facet, 11 recording the accepted EULA wording and 12 the citation format; the site methodology page matches.
Each result page and summary shows the citation line with the real version, id and permalink; a test checks one rendered page.
context:
Decision gate: if a managed service records neither tier nor size in existing bundles, it is unranked rather than guessed; the owner may later approve a tier mapping. Any corpus result whose rank changes is listed in the PR, not silently re-labelled.

Item guardrails: no edit to published bundles or sidecars; follow the explorer read-model version migration path (bump read_model_version, no hand-edited results.duckdb); site PR opens only after the core change merges and site inputs are republished; core and site one PR each.

Verification rubric: pass = all five acceptance points, the before/after counts, and the rehearsal site URL showing split cohorts and a citation. Fail = any result ranked without a hardware key, or a page without the citation.

Base guardrails: linked worktree, never the primary clone; no live-cloud runs or credentials; heavy work only via make heavy-run after make heavy-status; no deliberate host load; comment policy; changelog.d fragment.

2026-11-17 owner direction: hardware should be a TIERED key (CPUs and core counts of similar performance grouped) rather than exact model + cores, to split fewer cohorts. Measured on the corpus: exact model+cores splits 25 of 61 base cohorts (30 below 3 platforms); CPU family + core band with core counts filled from the model splits 6 (4 thin). The owner asked for a methodology based on public performance data; research is running and the owner picks the method before this item starts. The acceptance line defining the hardware key is superseded by that choice.
description:
Owner decisions 2026-11-17 on owner-confirm-provisional-decisions-20261117: the provisional methodology answers are confirmed, except hardware, which becomes a full ranking facet; the 'Derived from' wording is accepted as meeting EULA clause 4c(3); third parties cite as 'BenchBox <version>, result <public_result_id>, <permalink>, accessed <date>. Not an official TPC result.'

Corpus at 2026-11-17 (507 published results): 381 on one Apple M4 (10 cores), the rest on four cloud runner CPU models or with no recorded hardware (61, mostly managed services); 40 of 64 cohorts mix hardware, so the facet splits them and many fall below the 3-identity ranking minimum.

Outcome: rankings and comparisons group by hardware key; the ADR and site methodology page drop the provisional label and state the hardware rule, the EULA answer and the citation format; result pages show the citation.
